exposure: length of the second stage of labour
cohort: 36,662 nulliparous women delivering singleton, vertex, non-anomalous fetuses at term in Nova Scotia, Canada, from 2005 to 2019
finding: Increasing length of the second stage of labour was associated with increasing risk of OASIS overall, but the association was heterogeneous between modes of delivery.
mod_finding: Second stage length >= 90 min was associated with an increased OASIS risk in spontaneous and vacuum-assisted vaginal deliveries, while in forceps-assisted vaginal deliveries, OASIS risk was increased, with shorter and longer durations of the second stage.
